userStories.title: Eliminate duplicate json3 retry in caption format fallback sequence
acceptanceCriteria: Caption format fallback sequence does NOT repeat any format (no duplicate json3 at end)
When all formats fail for a video, total yt-dlp invocations is exactly len(unique_formats) not more
A new CaptionFormatExhaustedError is raised when all unique formats fail (not generic error)
Unit test verifies fallback tries each format exactly once then raises CaptionFormatExhaustedError
Unit test verifies no subprocess is spawned for a format that already failed in the same fetch cycle
userStories.notes: All 5 criteria verified. Dedup via dict.fromkeys at init and in _fetch_subtitle_formats. CaptionFormatExhaustedError in src/caption/exceptions.py. 15 tests in tests/test_format_dedup_exhaustion.py all pass.

userStories.title: Add format-level timeout budget across all caption format attempts
acceptanceCriteria: A configurable total_format_timeout_seconds field exists in CaptionFirstConfig (default: 60)
When cumulative time across ALL format attempts exceeds the budget, remaining formats are skipped
Skipped-due-to-timeout formats are logged with DEBUG level including elapsed vs budget
Unit test verifies budget enforcement: mock slow subprocess, confirm 3rd format is skipped when budget is 30s and first 2 took 16s each
Config field is documented in config.yaml with comment explaining the budget
userStories.notes: Tier: P1 performance. Files: src/caption_fetcher.py (lines ~4615-4695 _fetch_subtitle_formats), src/config/sections/download.py (CaptionFirstConfig). Currently each format attempt gets its own independent timeout (45s json3, 25s vtt/srt) with no shared budget. A video with no captions wastes up to 95s (45+25+25) before giving up. A shared timeout budget caps total wall-clock time spent on format attempts per video.

userStories.title: Audit and fix all subprocess calls missing encoding parameters
acceptanceCriteria: Every subprocess.run and subprocess.Popen call with text=True also has encoding='utf-8' and errors='replace'
Files audited: src/downloader/audio_first.py, src/downloader/title_filter.py, src/downloader/vpn_manager.py, src/downloader/speech_screening.py, src/caption_fetcher.py
grep for 'text=True' across src/ returns zero hits without accompanying encoding='utf-8'
Unit test in tests/test_subprocess_encoding.py uses ast module to parse all Python files in src/ and assert every subprocess.run/Popen call with text=True also has encoding kwarg
No functional behavior changes beyond encoding parameter addition
userStories.notes: Tier: P0 bug fix (Rule 27 compliance). Files: src/downloader/audio_first.py (~lines 347, 594, 784, 900), src/downloader/title_filter.py (~line 179), src/downloader/vpn_manager.py (~lines 172, 226), src/downloader/speech_screening.py (~line 66). Several subprocess calls are missing encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' which causes crashes on non-UTF8 yt-dlp output in Windows environments. The mullvad_vpn.py file already has correct encoding as a reference pattern.

userStories.title: Cache caption preflight discovery results to avoid repeated list-subs calls
acceptanceCriteria: Caption preflight results (available formats per video ID) are cached in caption_fetcher_cache with 1-hour TTL
On cache hit, _check_captions_preflight skips the yt-dlp --list-subs subprocess call entirely
Cache key format is '{video_id}_preflight' to distinguish from caption content cache entries
Unit test verifies second call for same video_id does not spawn subprocess (mock subprocess, check call count)
Unit test verifies cache entry expires after TTL and triggers fresh --list-subs call
userStories.notes: Tier: P1 performance. Files: src/caption_fetcher.py (lines ~2598-2750 _check_captions_preflight), src/caption_fetcher_cache.py. Currently every call to _check_captions_preflight runs yt-dlp --list-subs even if the same video was checked seconds ago. In batch processing with retries, this can duplicate 100+ subprocess calls. Cache results using existing caption_fetcher_cache infrastructure with a distinct key prefix.

userStories.title: Persist adaptive caption format ordering across pipeline runs
acceptanceCriteria: Adaptive format order (success rates per format) is saved to .cache/caption_format_stats.json at end of caption stage
On next pipeline run, saved format order is loaded and used as initial preferred_formats list
File format is JSON with structure: {format_name: {successes: int, failures: int, last_updated: ISO timestamp}}
Unit test verifies round-trip: compute order from stats, save to file, load from file, confirm order matches
Stale entries (older than 7 days) are excluded from ordering calculation
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 performance optimization. Files: src/caption_fetcher.py (lines ~2500-2537 apply_adaptive_format_order), src/stages/caption_stage.py. Currently adaptive format ordering is computed per-run based on in-memory success rates. Every pipeline run re-learns that e.g. vtt succeeds more often than json3. Persisting the stats file eliminates the re-learning phase and immediately uses the optimal format order.

userStories.title: Add exponential backoff to Mullvad VPN server rotation
acceptanceCriteria: VPN rotation delay increases exponentially: base_delay * 2^(rotation_count - 1) capped at max_rotation_delay_seconds
New config fields: initial_rotation_delay_seconds (default: 5), max_rotation_delay_seconds (default: 60) in MullvadConfig
When a rotation is followed by a successful download, the backoff counter resets to 0
Unit test verifies backoff progression: 5s, 10s, 20s, 40s, 60s (capped)
Unit test verifies backoff resets after success
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 resilience. Files: src/downloader/mullvad_vpn.py (lines ~200-270 rotate_server, ~line 116 _rotation_delay), src/config/sections/download.py (MullvadConfig). Currently VPN rotation uses a fixed delay (5s) regardless of whether rotation helped. If YouTube is rate-limiting at the account level (not IP level), rotating VPN servers won't help but wastes 5s per rotation. Exponential backoff reduces wasted time when rotations are ineffective.

userStories.title: Integrate download speed tracking into SegmentDownloadStats
acceptanceCriteria: SegmentDownloadStats has new field download_speeds: List[float] tracking bytes/second per segment
After each segment download, speed is calculated from bytes and elapsed time and appended to list
New method average_speed() returns mean download speed across all segments (or 0.0 if empty)
New method is_speed_degrading(window=5, threshold=0.5) returns True if last N speeds are below threshold of overall average
Unit test verifies speed tracking with mock download timings
Unit test verifies is_speed_degrading detects sustained slowdown
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 observability. Files: src/stages/download_segments.py (lines ~88-114 SegmentDownloadStats). The stats dataclass tracks total_bytes and counts but not download speed over time. Without speed tracking, the pipeline can't detect gradual throttling (download works but gets slower and slower). This enables future escalation triggers based on speed degradation rather than just outright failures.

userStories.title: Consolidate duplicate error classification between downloader and caption systems
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/common/error_patterns.py contains shared error severity patterns (403, 429, bot detection, etc.)
src/downloader/error_classification.py imports patterns from src/common/error_patterns.py instead of defining its own
src/caption/error_handling.py imports patterns from src/common/error_patterns.py instead of defining its own
All existing tests in tests/test_downloader_error_classification*.py and tests/test_caption_error*.py still pass
New unit test verifies that adding a pattern to shared module is picked up by both downloader and caption classifiers
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 code quality. Files: src/downloader/error_classification.py (ERROR_SEVERITY_PATTERNS), src/caption/error_handling.py (categorize_caption_error). Both modules have overlapping regex patterns for classifying yt-dlp errors (403, 429, bot detection, etc.) but maintain them independently. Changes to one don't propagate to the other, leading to inconsistent error handling. Extract shared patterns to a common module.

userStories.title: Extract common circuit breaker base class from download and caption implementations
acceptanceCriteria: New abstract base class src/common/circuit_breaker_base.py with shared state management (open/closed/half-open), failure counting, and jitter calculation
src/downloader/circuit_breaker.py inherits from base class, keeping only download-specific cascade logic
src/caption/circuit_breaker.py inherits from base class, keeping only caption-specific threshold logic
All existing circuit breaker tests pass without modification
Unit test for base class verifies state transitions: closed -> open (on threshold) -> half-open (on timeout) -> closed (on success)
userStories.notes: Tier: P2 code quality / DRY. Files: src/downloader/circuit_breaker.py (705 lines), src/caption/circuit_breaker.py. Both files implement nearly identical circuit breaker state machines with open/closed/half-open states, failure threshold tracking, and jitter-based cooldown. Extract shared behavior to reduce maintenance burden and prevent divergence. Keep domain-specific behavior (download cascade vs caption batch abort) in subclasses.

userStories.title: Add auto-generated caption fallback when manual captions unavailable
acceptanceCriteria: When manual captions (--write-sub) fail for all formats, fetcher attempts auto-generated captions (--write-auto-sub) before giving up
Auto-generated caption attempt uses the same format preference order as manual captions
Caption result object has new field is_auto_generated: bool (default False) to distinguish source
Unit test verifies auto-sub fallback triggers only after all manual formats fail
Unit test verifies is_auto_generated=True when auto-sub succeeds
Auto-generated captions are cached with a distinct cache key suffix '_autosub' to avoid confusion with manual captions
userStories.notes: Tier: P1 feature. Files: src/caption_fetcher.py (lines ~4615-4695 _fetch_subtitle_formats, ~4697-4793 _fetch_subtitle_with_format). Many YouTube videos lack manual captions but have auto-generated ones. Currently the fetcher only tries --write-sub and gives up if manual captions are unavailable, forcing an expensive Whisper transcription fallback. Adding --write-auto-sub as a secondary attempt can recover captions for a significant fraction of videos that currently fall through to transcription.
